themes_detail.label: Drinking complaints surge
themes_detail.summary: Public drinking complaints spiked to 6 this week, a 2,300% increase from the 8-week baseline average of 0.2 per week, signaling a potential new or rapidly escalating public consumption problem in Kingsbridge/Bedford Park.
evidence: 6 drinking complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 per week 8-week average (z-score: 13.28)
Represents a 2,300% spike, highest z-score among all detected anomalies
No prior context available; appears to be entirely new behavior in the district
reporting_angles: Ground-level reporting: where are these incidents concentrated? Parks, transit hubs, commercial streets?
Interview NYPD/precinct commander about enforcement strategy and whether this reflects new activity or new complaint behavior

themes_detail.label: Water system failures accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Water system complaints jumped to 40 this week, a 135% increase from the 8-week baseline average of 17 per week, suggesting infrastructure strain or contamination concerns requiring immediate DEP investigation.
evidence: 40 water system complaints THIS WEEK vs. 17.0 per week 8-week average (z-score: 4.07)
135% spike occurring simultaneously with broader heat/hot water crisis (5,304 complaints over 90 days)
Water leak complaints also elevated at 524 over 90 days; plumbing at 867, suggesting system-wide strain
reporting_angles: Contact DEP: is there a specific water main break, contamination, or pressure issue in Kingsbridge/Bedford Park this week?
Cross-reference with Con Edison: are heat complaints correlated with water heating system failures?

themes_detail.label: Consumer complaints spike
themes_detail.summary: Consumer complaints surged to 23 this week, a 217% increase from the 8-week baseline average of 7.2 per week, indicating potential fraud, price gouging, or predatory business practices targeting district residents.
evidence: 23 consumer complaints THIS WEEK vs. 7.2 per week 8-week average (z-score: 4.66)
217% spike is among the freshest anomalies detected
Mobile food vendor complaints also spiked 433% 3 weeks ago (4 vs. 0.8 avg); suggests business/vendor sector issues
reporting_angles: DCWP data request: what types of consumer complaints? Housing, food, services, price gouging?
Interview residents: are there new scams, landlord retaliation, or predatory vendors operating in the district this week?

themes_detail.label: Encampment spike 3 weeks ago
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints jumped to 16 three weeks ago, a 574% increase from the 8-week baseline average of 2.4 per week, reflecting a surge in unsheltered homelessness that community board has repeatedly requested DHS services to address.
evidence: 16 encampment complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 2.4 per week 8-week average (z-score: 5.69)
574% spike; community board has repeatedly budgeted for 'Other request for services for the homeless' (DHS) suggesting chronic unmet need
Spike timing predates current week, but remains unresolved; no follow-up data available on whether encampments have been cleared
reporting_angles: Canvass parks and known encampment sites: are the 16 reported encampments still present? Have conditions worsened?
Interview DHS/Bronx Borough Commissioner: what outreach and services were deployed 3 weeks ago in response to spike?

themes_detail.label: Unsanitary condition complaints drop sharply
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary condition complaints declined 40% to 57 this week from the 8-week baseline average of 95.1 per week, a statistically significant drop (z-score: -6.95) that may indicate improved enforcement, under-reporting, or community fatigue.
evidence: 57 unsanitary condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 95.1 per week 8-week average (z-score: -6.95, DOWN 40%)
Despite drop, unsanitary conditions remain #4 complaint category over 90-day period (1,244 total)
Counterintuitive trend: heat complaints remain elevated (5,304 over 90 days), typically correlate with sanitation issues
reporting_angles: Sanitation Department data request: did enforcement operations increase this week? Were summonses issued?
Check if lower complaints reflect improved conditions, reduced street activity due to heat, or complaint fatigue among residents
